subject: EN
prompt: **17.** Why did the council first think about switching off the street lights?

choices: to spend less money
to make the stars visible again
to protect insects
because villagers had complained about the light

explanation.title: Beleg im Text
explanation.body: Absatz 2: *The idea did not come from star lovers. It came from the village council's accountant … lighting the empty streets … was costing more than the council spent on its library.* Sterne und Insekten kommen erst später im Text, als Folge.
Teile den Artikel in Abschnitte ein, markiere die Schlüsselwörter der Frage (*council, first*) und suche sie im passenden Abschnitt.

source: Eigene Aufgabe im Format MSA Englisch, Reading Part 3

subject: EN
prompt: **18.** The money saved during the trial was meant to …

choices: support places for readers and young people.
pay the council's accountant.
buy modern street lamps.
repair the road to the pub.

solution.correct_choice: support places for readers and young people.

explanation.title: Beleg im Text
explanation.body: Absatz 2: *The money saved would go to the library and the youth club.* → *library* = Ort für Leser, *youth club* = Ort für junge Leute.
Die richtige Antwort wiederholt den Text selten wörtlich. Sie sagt dasselbe mit anderen Wörtern.

source: Eigene Aufgabe im Format MSA Englisch, Reading Part 3

subject: EN
prompt: **19.** Sam Okoro was against the plan because …

choices: he was worried about his employees' way home.
he feared he would lose customers.
the people affected had not been asked.
both A + C

explanation.title: Beleg im Text
explanation.body: Absatz 3: *My staff walk home after closing time* (A) **und** *Nobody asked them how they feel* (C). Von Gästen, die wegbleiben, sagt er nichts.
Bei *both A + C* müssen **beide** Aussagen im Text belegt sein. Prüfe jede einzeln.

source: Eigene Aufgabe im Format MSA Englisch, Reading Part 3

subject: EN

choices: the darkness did not lead to more crime.
burglars prefer to work at night.
there were fewer break-ins than before.
thieves often carry torches in the afternoon.

solution.correct_choice: the darkness did not lead to more crime.

explanation.title: Beleg im Text
explanation.body: Absatz 4: *the number of break-ins … did not rise; it stayed exactly the same, at three.* Achtung: **gleich viele**, nicht weniger. Und: *Most burglaries … happen in the afternoon*, also gerade nicht nachts.
Zahlenfalle: *did not rise* heißt nicht *fell*. Lies genau, ob etwas steigt, sinkt oder gleich bleibt.

source: Eigene Aufgabe im Format MSA Englisch, Reading Part 3

subject: EN

choices: the dark nights were good for insects.
moths are more important than bees.
bats avoid villages without lamps.
street lamps help moths to find flowers.

solution.correct_choice: the dark nights were good for insects.

explanation.title: Beleg im Text
explanation.body: Absatz 5: *In the dark year we caught nearly twice as many moths in our traps.* Lampen **hindern** die Falter am Fressen (*instead of feeding and visiting flowers*). Dass Falter wichtiger als Bienen sind, sagt sie nicht – nur, dass auch nachts bestäubt wird.
Namen sind Anker: Suche *Whitlock* im Text und lies nur, was sie sagt.

source: Eigene Aufgabe im Format MSA Englisch, Reading Part 3

subject: EN
prompt: **22.** What does Whitlock say about the sleep survey?

choices: Its result should not be trusted too much.
It proves that darkness improves sleep.
Too few villagers took part in it.
It was carried out by doctors.

solution.correct_choice: Its result should not be trusted too much.

explanation.title: Beleg im Text
explanation.body: Absatz 6: *Whitlock is careful with this number … People who like the project may simply want it to be true. We asked for opinions. We did not measure anybody's sleep.* → Meinungen sind kein Beweis.
Achte auf Signalwörter wie *though, however, careful*: Danach kommt eine Einschränkung.

source: Eigene Aufgabe im Format MSA Englisch, Reading Part 3

subject: EN
prompt: **23.** How was the conflict in the village solved?

choices: Some lamps now switch on only when they are needed.
All lamps were switched on again.
The pub now closes earlier.
The council pays for taxis after midnight.

solution.correct_choice: Some lamps now switch on only when they are needed.

explanation.title: Beleg im Text
explanation.body: Absatz 7: *The lamps on the road between the pub and the bus stop were fitted with sensors: they now stay off until somebody walks by, then light up for three minutes.*

source: Eigene Aufgabe im Format MSA Englisch, Reading Part 3

subject: EN
prompt: **24.** At the end of the trial, Sam Okoro …

choices: accepts the solution.
still criticises how the decision was made.
wants to start a new petition.
both A + B

explanation.title: Beleg im Text
explanation.body: Absatz 7: *Okoro took down his petition … my staff get home safely* (A) **und** *I still think they should have talked to us first* (B). Eine neue Unterschriftenliste plant er nicht.
*still* zeigt: Etwas hat sich nicht geändert. *But* danach zeigt, was sich doch geändert hat.

source: Eigene Aufgabe im Format MSA Englisch, Reading Part 3

subject: EN
prompt: **25.** Another title for this article could be …

choices: Lights out: how a village learned to like the dark
Why modern villages need more street lamps
The end of crime in the countryside
A beginner's guide to watching the stars

solution.correct_choice: Lights out: how a village learned to like the dark

explanation.title: Beleg im Text
explanation.body: Der ganze Artikel erzählt den Versuch von Anfang (Absatz 1–2) über den Streit (3) und die Ergebnisse (4–6) bis zur Einigung (7–8). Kriminalität und Sterne sind nur einzelne Abschnitte.
Ein Titel muss zum **ganzen** Text passen, nicht nur zu einem Absatz.

source: Eigene Aufgabe im Format MSA Englisch, Reading Part 3

subject: EN
prompt: **17.** What has changed at Threadbare over the last fifteen years?

choices: Customers are no longer embarrassed to shop there.
The shop now sells only new clothes.
Older customers have replaced the young ones.
Filming inside the shop is no longer allowed.

solution.correct_choice: Customers are no longer embarrassed to shop there.

explanation.title: Beleg im Text
explanation.body: Absatz 1: *Fifteen years ago, people came in here quietly and hoped nobody from school would see them … Now they film themselves at the till.* Früher heimlich, heute zeigen sie es allen.
Die erste Frage zielt fast immer auf den Einstieg des Artikels. Suche das Gegensatzpaar *Fifteen years ago … Now …*.

source: Eigene Aufgabe im Format MSA Englisch, Reading Part 3

subject: EN
prompt: **18.** Which reason(s) for buying second-hand clothes does the text mention?

choices: low prices
good quality
the wish to look different from others
all of them (A+B+C)

explanation.title: Beleg im Text
explanation.body: Absatz 2: *costs a fraction of a new one* (A), *often better made than the cheap fashion* (B), *unlikely that anyone else in class will turn up wearing the same thing* (C).
*all of them* ist nur richtig, wenn du **jeden** einzelnen Punkt im Text findest. Hake sie einzeln ab.

source: Eigene Aufgabe im Format MSA Englisch, Reading Part 3

subject: EN
prompt: **19.** For many young shoppers, the most important reason is that second-hand clothes …

choices: are better for the environment.
are easy to find online.
are worn by celebrities.
can be sold again later.

explanation.title: Beleg im Text
explanation.body: Absatz 2: *the strongest argument is a different one: every item that is worn again is one that does not have to be produced, transported and … thrown away.* → weniger Herstellung, Transport und Müll.
*most important* → suche im Text ein Wort mit gleicher Bedeutung: *the strongest argument*.

source: Eigene Aufgabe im Format MSA Englisch, Reading Part 3

subject: EN

choices: has almost completely stopped buying new clothes.
works at Threadbare on Saturdays.
sells his old jeans on apps.
only shops online.

solution.correct_choice: has almost completely stopped buying new clothes.

explanation.title: Beleg im Text
explanation.body: Absatz 3: *He has not bought anything new for a year, apart from socks and underwear.* → fast nichts Neues. Auf Apps **kauft** er, vom Verkaufen steht nichts da; und die meisten Sachen findet er im Laden.
Kleine Wörter entscheiden: *apart from* (außer), *most* (die meisten), *the rest* (der Rest).

source: Eigene Aufgabe im Format MSA Englisch, Reading Part 3

subject: EN
prompt: **21.** What does Priya Nair criticise about some app users?

choices: They leave nothing for people with little money.
They break the law.
They sell fake brand clothes.
They steal from charity shops.

solution.correct_choice: They leave nothing for people with little money.

explanation.title: Beleg im Text
explanation.body: Absatz 4: *the people who really need a warm coat for five pounds now find an empty rail.* Ausdrücklich: *They are not doing anything illegal.*
Wenn eine Antwort das Gegenteil eines Satzes im Text behauptet, ist sie falsch – auch wenn das Wort (*illegal*) im Text vorkommt.

source: Eigene Aufgabe im Format MSA Englisch, Reading Part 3

subject: EN
prompt: **22.** Dr Hofmann's study shows that teenagers who buy second-hand …

choices: often buy more than they need.
own fewer clothes than other teenagers.
wear every item many times.
spend more money than others.

solution.correct_choice: often buy more than they need.

explanation.title: Beleg im Text
explanation.body: Absatz 5: *Those who mostly bought second-hand owned more items, not fewer … One in four pieces had been worn only once or never.*
*more items, not fewer*: Der Text betont den Vergleich selbst. Solche Stellen werden gern abgefragt.

source: Eigene Aufgabe im Format MSA Englisch, Reading Part 3

subject: EN
prompt: **23.** Why is the boom a problem for charity shops?

choices: They are given a lot of clothes they cannot sell.
Dealing with useless donations costs them money.
They no longer receive enough donations.
both A + B

explanation.title: Beleg im Text
explanation.body: Absatz 6: *much of it is cheap fashion that … cannot be sold again* (A) **und** *Sorting it and getting rid of it costs the shops money* (B). C ist das Gegenteil: *more donations than ever*.
Bei *both A + B* müssen **beide** Aussagen belegt sein. Fehlt schon eine, ist die Kombination falsch.

source: Eigene Aufgabe im Format MSA Englisch, Reading Part 3

subject: EN

choices: thinking carefully before buying something
buying new clothes again
staying away from charity shops
paying the full price for used clothes

explanation.title: Beleg im Text
explanation.body: Absatz 7: *Her advice is simply to ask one question before paying: would I buy this at full price?* Sie rät nicht, den vollen Preis zu zahlen – die Frage ist nur ein Test. Und: *Buying used is still far better than buying new.*
*recommend* → suche *advice, should, suggest*. Dahinter steht der Rat.

source: Eigene Aufgabe im Format MSA Englisch, Reading Part 3

subject: EN
prompt: **25.** The focus of the text is on …

choices: the good and bad sides of a fashion trend.
the history of a second-hand shop.
how to earn money with used clothes.
the amount of water needed to make jeans.

solution.correct_choice: the good and bad sides of a fashion trend.

explanation.title: Beleg im Text
explanation.body: Der rote Faden: Absatz 1–3 zeigen, warum gebrauchte Kleidung beliebt ist; Absatz 4–6 zeigen die Probleme (Weiterverkäufer, zu viel kaufen, unbrauchbare Spenden); Absatz 7–8 ziehen ein Fazit. Threadbare ist nur der Aufhänger.
Für die Frage nach dem Schwerpunkt zählst du, welches Thema in den **meisten** Absätzen vorkommt – nicht, womit der Text beginnt.
